Open Day Tours
We shall be hosting three Open Day sessions for any prospective parents/carers thinking of joining Holy Ghost Primary School in 2027/2028.
Thursday 22nd October 2026 at 9.15am-10.15am
Thursday 12th November 2026 at 9.15am-10.15am
Thursday 10th December 2026 at 9.15am-10.15am
There will be welcome message from our Executive Head / Head of School, followed by a tour of the school with our Year 6 pupils.
If you would book a place on an Open Day tour, please click here

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Ghost Primary School - RE Curriculum
pageCache.text:
RE Curriculum
Religious Education at Holy Ghost
At the heart of our school, is our Catholic mission, which gives us our identity as a school and reaches into every aspect of our work.
In keeping with our mission statement, we aim to work alongside parents to bring children to a deeper understanding of the truths of their Catholic faith.
Through explicit teaching about Jesus and the Church, and the development of prayer and worship in school, we provide daily experiences where children live the gospel values; have respect for the opinions and beliefs of others, and grow in their faith.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Ghost Primary School - Catholic Schools' Inspectorate Report
pageCache.text:
Catholic Schools' Inspectorate Report
Catholic Schools’ Inspectorate Inspection (CSI), Dec’ 2025
Overall judgement - Outstanding
This is a wonderful achievement for our entire school community and stands as a testament to the remarkable dedication of our pupils, staff, parents/carers, clergy and all who contribute to the life of Holy Ghost. The inspectors highlighted the culture of inclusivity at the heart of our school, noting how our children flourish within our Catholic ethos. Inspectors also commended the exceptional relationships and pastoral care, which ensure that each child feels valued as a unique creation of God.
At Holy Ghost, we place great value not only on academic excellence, but also on the moral and spiritual development of our pupils and are delighted that this integral aspect of our mission has been recognised and celebrated in such a positive way.
This achievement is a wonderful reflection of the collective effort and commitment of our entire school community and testament to the commitment of the Religious Leaders, who were highly commended by the Inspectors for their skills, experience and dedication.
Please click here to read the full report.
Catholic Life and Mission - Outstanding
Religious Education - Outstanding
Collective Worship - Outstanding

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Ghost Primary School - Catholic Social Teaching
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching is rooted in scripture, challenging us to live responsibly and build a just society, putting our faith into action.
CAFOD Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching with CAFOD video
Our School Catholic Social Teaching Initiatives
At Holy Ghost, our Catholic values are at the core in everything we do. Each term we are focusing on one of the core Catholic Social Teaching values, where one class leads a whole school initiative to support those in need.
In the Autumn 1 term our focus is on Human Dignity.
In Autumn 2 term our focus is on Solidarity.
In the Spring 1 term our focus is on The Common Good.
In the Spring 2 term our focus is on Preferential Option of the Poor.
In the Summer 1 term our focus is on Stewardship.
In the Summer 2 term our focus is on Participation.
Big Lent Walk
During this Lenten season, our hard-working Chaplains have organised for the whole school to participate in CAFOD's Big Lent Walk. We are taking time during Lent to reflect on the Catholic Social Teaching Value of the Preferential Option for the Poor - our obligation to put people most in need first. Three times a week, the children will walk or run with their class, in solidarity with those who walk miles each day to access safe water. The children are hoping to raise money to bring clean, safe water to communities around the world.
We have set up a fundraising page on the CAFOD schools site here:
https://schools.walk.cafod.org.uk/
There is a QR code or link to the Just Giving website.
This Lenten challenge is really important to us, and your support would be very much appreciated!
Senior Parishioner Coffee Morning, Tuesday 2nd December 2025
We were delighted to host our senior parishioners to a special Coffee Morning on Tuesday, 2nd December. Following the 9.30am Mass, our Year 6 pupils hosted the event and shared some of the wonderful learning they have been doing in RE and Literacy. Year 6 enjoyed chatting with the parishioners, making tea and coffee! We look forward to hosting the event next year!
Toiletry Drive for the East Hill Supper Food Bank - October 2025
This half term, we are putting our Catholic Social Teaching value of Dignity into action through a special appeal to support the East Hill Supper Food Bank, in partnership with our local Holy Ghost Parish.
Rather than collecting food items, we are focusing on toiletries — everyday essentials that are often overlooked but deeply needed. By donating these items, we uphold the dignity of those in our community who are experiencing hardship.
A huge thank you to everyone who kindly donated much-needed toiletries to our Food Bank appeal. Thanks to your incredible generosity, over 1,000 items were collected!
The CST Chaplains were busy sorting through all the donations today, and these items will be delivered to the Food Bank this afternoon. The car boot and backseat were overflowing.
Your support will make a real difference to local families in need — thank you for showing such wonderful community spirit!
Year 1
Year 1 have been learning all about Pope Francis's encyclical Laudato Si' and thinking about being more like Sophia the Sloth, who teaches us to be a great steward by caring about our world. We have been making bug hotels and planting vegetables and bulbs.
Catholic Social Teaching Values
We have begun our school year by reflecting on the importance of the Catholic Social Teaching values, and how we enrich our relationships and the life of our school when we use them.
The new school year has just begun, and we are already full of great ideas! We’re excited to think about ways we can live out our passion for Catholic Social Teaching here at Holy Ghost School.
Our first initiative is to work together with Holy Ghost Parish to support their call for donations to the Food Bank. This project helps us think about the importance of Human Dignity—making sure every person has what they need to live with respect and care.
We’ll be sharing more information soon, so stay tuned!
Participation - 10th July 2025
Year 4 hosted a fantastic art show based on the Catholic Social Teaching of Participation. Children from across the school contributed their artwork, and it was lovely to see so many families enjoying the display. We had a great range of artwork and very impressive 3D models. Thank you to everyone who donated.
We raised over £75.00 for our selected charity, Aid to the Church in Need. Thank you to everyone who donated.
Stewardship
Year 1 - Alongside our RE learning inside the classroom, we have also been busy in our school garden. The children have been carefully watering the vegetables and fruit we’ve been growing and observing how they are changing over time. This hands-on work has helped us live out another important Catholic Social Teaching value, taught by Sofia the Sloth — stewardship. We have been learning how to care for God’s creation and appreciate the world around us by looking after our plants and using resources wisely.
As part of our focus on the CST value of stewardship, we are thinking about ways to keep our area of London clean and tidy. During May children in Year 2 joined Beautify Balham to pick up litter from the local streets. They were amazed and proud of the amount of litter they have picked up.

Advent Food Drive
One of the ways that we have prepared during this special season is the Advent Food Drive. Thank you to all families who donated much needed items to the Wandsworth Food Bank. Senior Parishioners Coffee Morning
This term, our school CST focus this term is Solidarity. We have been teaching the children to reflect on HOW they can show others they care and explaining that we are connected to people and places all over the world. God created us for one global family and wants us to support all of our brothers and sisters.
Big Lent Walk
This term, our focus in Catholic Social Teaching has been the Preferential Option for the Poor. Through Scripture, we have learned that Jesus calls us to care for those most in need and to always put the poorest first.
Year 3 are taking their turn to lead this important mi
ssion by organising a fundraising walk for the Catholic Children's Society. They have worked hard to create banners and promote the event, encouraging everyone to take part. It has been truly inspiring to see classes coming together each week, walking with enthusiasm and increasing their laps to support this worthy cause.
This initiative not only helps raise money for those in need but also reminds us of the importance of compassion, generosity, and acting on our faith. We are so proud of Year 3 for their leadership and dedication in making a difference in the lives of others.
The Passage - school visit
On Wednesday 19th March 2025, we were fortunate enough to have a visit from The Passage, a charity dedicated to preventing and ending homelessness in London. They led a whole school assembly, raising awareness about homelessness and asking our pupils to consider how they can contribute positively to our community. This visit emphasised the importance of compassion and service to others, linking with our Catholic Social Teaching focus: Option for the Poor.
